claim_being_audited: The Actor claims that certifying the model is defensible because aggregate performance clears the deployment threshold, but only if the audit packet explicitly discloses the small-business support slice weakness and its uncertainty, since no approved mitigation has removed exposure.
specific_concerns: The admissible evidence supports aggregate launch readiness and shows an unresolved weak slice, but it does not establish the missing policy predicate that this slice weakness materially affects a protected or contractual customer segment.

The Actor states the weakness 'must be disclosed' as a settled conclusion, but the available evidence does not prove materiality; the policy text itself treats unresolved materiality as not equivalent to clean certification.
The recommendation to certify is stronger than the evidence supports because the certification condition depends on a disclosure trigger that is not fully evidenced in the packet.
unsupported_claims: The claim that the small-business support slice weakness must be disclosed is not fully supported because material effect on a protected or contractual customer segment is not established in admissible evidence.
The claim that certification is affirmatively defensible on this record is overclaimed absent evidence resolving the materiality predicate.
evidence_requests: Evidence that the small-business support slice is a protected or contractual customer segment under the disclosure policy.
Evidence that the observed weakness may materially affect that segment, not merely that it is below warning and preferred thresholds.
Any approved materiality determination, risk review, or policy interpretation tying this slice result to mandatory model-card disclosure.
decision_criteria: Aggregate threshold clearance can support overall launch readiness.
Subgroup weakness is not erased by aggregate pass rates.
Disclosure is mandatory only if the weakness may materially affect a protected or contractual customer segment, unless an approved mitigation removes exposure.
A draft mitigation that is not approved does not remove exposure.
Small-sample uncertainty supports follow-up confirmation but does not resolve an otherwise missing policy predicate.
